cmb.description: CMB temperature and polarisation, lensing, Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effects, spectral distortions, foregrounds and experiments.
cmb.guidance:
On theme: papers whose main subject is the CMB or its secondary anisotropies.
Off theme: papers that only use CMB data as one input to another analysis.
Impact: as for cosmology.
cmb.name: cmb
cmb.title: Cosmic microwave background

cosmology.description: Cosmological models and parameters, large-scale structure, the cosmic microwave background, dark matter and dark energy.
cosmology.name: cosmology
cosmology.title: Cosmology and dark matter

cosmology-non-cmb.description: Cosmology from large-scale structure, weak lensing, clusters, supernovae, BAO, line-intensity mapping, gravitational waves and dark matter, excluding CMB studies.
cosmology-non-cmb.guidance:
On theme: any astro-ph.CO paper whose main subject is not the CMB.
Off theme: papers whose main subject is the CMB (they belong to the CMB theme);
papers that only use CMB data in a combination stay on theme.
Impact: 3 = new cosmological constraints from a major survey or data release, or a
result that changes a known tension; 2 = solid new measurement or method; 1 = incremental.
cosmology-non-cmb.name: cosmology-non-cmb
cosmology-non-cmb.title: Cosmology (non-CMB)

galactic-archaeology.description: Structure, assembly history, chemistry and dynamics of the Milky Way from large stellar surveys: halo, discs and bulge, accreted populations and merger history.
galactic-archaeology.name: galactic-archaeology
galactic-archaeology.title: Galactic archaeology

galaxy-dynamics.description: Dynamics of galaxies and of the Milky Way: potentials, orbits, bars and spirals, resonances, disc heating, dark matter haloes from kinematics, N-body methods.
galaxy-dynamics.guidance:
On theme: papers whose main subject is the dynamics of galaxies or of the Milky Way.
Off theme: papers using kinematics only to classify objects; black hole accretion.
Impact: 3 = a new dynamical measurement of the Milky Way or galaxies with broad
consequences (potential, dark matter halo, bar), or a major method; 2 = solid
new result; 1 = incremental.
galaxy-dynamics.name: galaxy-dynamics
galaxy-dynamics.title: Galaxy dynamics

galaxy-formation.description: How galaxies form and evolve across cosmic time: star formation, quenching, feedback, mergers, dwarf galaxies, the circumgalactic medium and high-redshift galaxies.
galaxy-formation.name: galaxy-formation
galaxy-formation.title: Galaxy formation and evolution

journals.name: The New England Journal of Medicine

science-at-large.description: Major research results of the period in any scientific field, published in leading general-science journals.
science-at-large.name: science-at-large
science-at-large.title: Science at large

stellar-streams.description: Detection, modelling and dynamics of stellar streams and tidal tails in the Milky Way and nearby galaxies, their progenitors (globular clusters, dwarf galaxies), and their use to constrain the Galactic potential, the dark matter halo and its substructure.
stellar-streams.name: stellar-streams
stellar-streams.title: Stellar streams

stream-observations.description: Detecting and characterising stellar streams and tidal features in photometric surveys, the impact of observational systematics on these measurements, and major advances against survey systematics (large-scale structure, star-galaxy separation).
stream-observations.guidance:
On theme:
- Detection, mapping and characterisation of streams and tidal features with
  photometric surveys (Gaia, DES, DELVE, Legacy Surveys, HSC, Rubin/LSST, Euclid, Roman),
  in the Milky Way first, and around external galaxies.
- Studies of how observational systematics (depth variations, extinction, photometric
  errors, star-galaxy separation, crowding, calibration, completeness) affect stream or
  stellar-halo measurements.
- Major methods or data products that reduce survey systematics in large-scale
  structure or star-galaxy separation.
Off theme: papers that only apply standard systematics corrections; cosmology results
whose main topic is not the systematics themselves.
Impact: 3 = a new survey, catalogue or method likely to change stream work, or a
quantified systematic with clear consequences; 2 = solid new detections or analysis;
1 = incremental.
stream-observations.name: stream-observations
stream-observations.title: Observing streams and survey systematics

streams-dark-matter.description: Using stellar streams to constrain dark matter (subhalo impacts, gaps, spurs, density and velocity fluctuations, dark matter models), and the stream dynamics that can mimic or hide those signatures.
streams-dark-matter.guidance:
On theme:
- Dark matter constraints or forecasts from streams: gaps, spurs, density power
  spectra, velocity dispersion, subhalo impacts, dark matter models (WDM, FDM, SIDM, PBH).
- Stream dynamics that are astrophysical systematics for dark matter studies: the host
  potential (disk, bar, spiral arms, LMC, halo shape, time evolution), giant molecular
  clouds, progenitor properties, epicyclic overdensities, chaos, stream-modelling methods.
- Milky Way streams first; streams around external galaxies are on theme too.
Off theme: detection or survey papers with no dark matter or dynamics analysis (they
belong to the next theme); cold gas flows, tidal disruption events, solar wind.
Relevance: 3 = a dark matter constraint or forecast from streams, or a perturbation
systematic quantified for such studies; 2 = stream dynamics or modelling useful to
dark matter inference; 1 = streams are context only. Prefer Milky Way work at equal fit.
streams-dark-matter.name: streams-dark-matter
streams-dark-matter.title: Stellar streams as dark matter probes
